title: Teach Me, My God and King
description: Teach Me, My God and King in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 302, “All Work Divine”, where the book credits them to the Chr. Psalmist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Teach me, my God and King, In all things Thee to see; And what I do in a-ny-thing, To do it as for Thee!

lines: Teach me, my God and King,
In all things Thee to see;
And what I do in anything,
To do it as for Thee!
While still to Thee I tend;
In all I do be Thou the way;
In all be Thou the end.
But draws, when acted for Thy sake,
Hallowed is toil, if this the cause;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
